entries.grounds: At the snapshot the mutant is run.py:142 `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="aisef-check-")` -> prefix=''. Only the basename of the --check clone's scratch directory changes (aisef-check-<8> -> <8>, drawn from [a-z0-9_], measured over 300 names: never a leading '-', always absolute, so `git -C <tmp>` at run.py:143 cannot read it as an option). Nothing branches on the name; the TemporaryDirectory handle removes the directory either way (workspace.py:5-7: 'a scratch directory is removed by the TemporaryDirectory handle that created it' — the name carries no deletion authority). The name reaches operator-read text in two refusals: run.py:144-145 'the project repository could not be cloned: <git stderr[:200]>' (stderr = workspace.py:64-71 'refused: the repository configuration at <tmp> names K (not inert)' when TMPDIR lies in a repository whose own configuration holds a key INERT_KEY does not list — reproduced here with TMPDIR inside a repo with core.hooksPath: both variants refuse with the same RunRefused text but for the directory name; with this host's long scratch TMPDIR the 200-character cut falls inside the path in both variants) and run.py:147-149 `RunRefused(held.stderr)` (same text with <tmp>/repo; the clone-carries-the-key trigger I derived from workspace.py:64-71, I did not find an in-tree way to trigger it independently). Both go through cli.py:92-94 'aisef run: refused: ...', exit 2, nothing parses the text. What the operator acts on (the cause class, 'refused', the key, '(not inert)', the exit status) is carried unchanged; what goes is the word that says the path is --check's own scratch clone and not their repository, in a path that no longer exists when the message is read. The refusal that does name the operator's repository ('does not hold the plan's baseline') uses `shown or repo` (run.py:151) and never carries the scratch name. No requirement promises the label; the only possible test is 'the message contains aisef-check-', a verbatim-label test.
